definitions.gloss: nonpartisan; independent; not affiliated with any political party
definitions.explanation: Not belonging to or supporting any particular political party. Used to describe both politicians who run without party affiliation and voters who do not consistently support one party.

examples.japanese: {無党派|むとうは}⟦{層|そう}→層：12441_sou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{票|ひょう}→票：03582_hyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{選挙|せんきょ}→選挙：03303_senkyo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鍵|かぎ}→鍵：02189_kagi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{握|にぎ}る→握る：02383_nigiru⟧。
examples.english: The votes of independent voters hold the key to the election.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{無党派|むとうは}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{立候補|りっこうほ}→立候補：13778_rikkouho⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He ran as an independent candidate.

examples.japanese: ⟦{若者|わかもの}→若者：03037_wakamono⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{間|あいだ}→間：00914_aida⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{無党派|むとうは}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: Among young people, the number of those with no party affiliation is growing.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{無|む}→無：17750_mu⟧ (without) and ⟦{党派|とうは}→党派：23147_touha⟧ (political party/faction). A key term in Japanese election coverage, as {無党派|むとうは}⟦{層|そう}→層：12441_sou⟧ (the independent voter bloc) often determines election outcomes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無党派|むとうは}⟦{層|そう}→層：12441_sou⟧: independent voters; swing voters
- {無党派|むとうは}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{立候補|りっこうほ}→立候補：13778_rikkouho⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to run as an independent
- {無党派|むとうは}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{有権者|ゆうけんしゃ}→有権者：13021_yuukensha⟧: nonpartisan voters
- {無党派|むとうは}⟦{候補|こうほ}→候補：02804_kouho⟧: independent candidate

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{無所属|むしょぞく}→無所属：13583_mushozoku⟧: unaffiliated; independent — specifically about formal organizational membership
- ⟦{中立|ちゅうりつ}→中立：11324_chuuritsu⟧: neutral — broader, not limited to politics
- {浮動票|ふどうひょう}: floating votes; swing votes — the votes themselves, not the voters

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese politics, the {無党派|むとうは}⟦{層|そう}→層：12441_sou⟧ has grown significantly since the 1990s, reflecting voter disillusionment with established parties. Poll results often report the percentage of respondents who identify as {無党派|むとうは}.
